# Temple Scroll Column 57 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 57 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**57:1** When the king takes the throne of his kingdom, a copy of this Torah must be written for him on a scroll, copied from the one kept by the priests.

**57:2** This is the Torah they must write for him: he must not [...] and he must not add to My commands or take anything away from them.

**57:3** He must read it every day of his life, so he will learn to honor Me and to carefully obey every word of this Torah.

**57:4** He must not think of himself as better than his fellow Israelites, and he must not deviate from My commands in any way,

**57:5** so that he and his descendants after him may enjoy a long reign over Israel.

**57:6** He must choose from his fellow Israelites one thousand men from each tribe to serve as his personal guard — twelve thousand trained soldiers in all —

**57:7** who must never leave him unprotected, in case he is captured by foreign enemies.

**57:8** Every man he selects must be trustworthy, God-fearing, honest, and courageous.

**57:9** They must stay with him at all times, day and night, protecting him from any wrongdoing

**57:10** and from any foreign entanglement, so he does not fall into enemy hands.

**57:11** He must also have an advisory council made up of twelve leaders from among the people, twelve priests, and twelve Levites —

**57:12** who will sit with him to decide matters of justice and interpret the Torah.

**57:13** He must not consider himself above them, and he must never make any decision without consulting them first.

**57:14** He must not marry a foreign woman. He must choose his wife from his own family, from his father's household.

**57:15** He must not take a second wife while his first wife is alive, for she alone shall be his companion for life.

**57:16** Only if she dies may he marry again, and his new wife must also come from his father's household and family.

**57:17** He must not twist justice, accept bribes, or covet anyone's field, vineyard, property, house, or any possession in Israel.

**57:18** He must not confiscate [...] anything belonging to the people.

**57:19** He must not hoard silver and gold beyond what is needed — only enough for his requirements.

**57:20** When the war trumpet sounds, he must lead his troops into battle; and when the assembly trumpet sounds, they must rally to him.

**57:21** He must consult with his council before acting, and must never go to war without their advice.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 57 presents the Temple Scroll's distinctive royal legislation. The 12,000-man guard, the 36-member council, and the strict monogamy law are all unique to this text. The king is thoroughly constrained — he cannot act without his council, cannot marry foreigners or multiple wives, and cannot accumulate wealth. This represents a radical vision of limited monarchy under divine Torah.*
